methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series winning with 54 series units?
How should adherence be measured when the recommendation is derived from the same play-by-play data?
Does the recommendation's own construction leak outcome information into the adherence measure?
What sample size, base-rate, and confounding (team quality) conditions are needed for a credible test?

historical_evidence.finding: Compared observed play-type mix with the recommended opener in single 2025-26 playoff G1s (4 games x 2 offenses). Avg |delta| on leverage buckets was 4.5pp to 24.0pp; 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. Recorded as descriptive, with no outcome comparison, and a MECHANICAL_FLOOR risk from muted CUT and PNR (tagger floor).

Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 (inflated n, team-quality confound); series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 with n=50, underpowered, with the record stating about 80 series are needed for p<0.05. Low AVOID-share bin 52.6% vs 25-50% bin 37.0%. Still confounded by team quality. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Ranked playsheet validation over 10 series: Spearman rho=-0.0639 p=0.099717 n=665 (no full-rank signal). Kruskal-Wallis H=32.97 p=2.7e-05. Mann-Whitney BEST 1.257 (n=56) vs AVOID 1.092 (n=160) p=0.004. Trigger accuracy rho=0.4525 n=121. Limited by leakage, low measurement reliability and small sample; DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY also flagged.

Audit of an overnight LLM batch claiming 'adaptation predicts series winners 9/10'. The audit found 706 findings with n<5, series winners never looked up (0/2073 calls), LLM-inferred winners, an invented game score, and point costs from LLM arithmetic. Classified C_artifact. Related to the same winning-claim type but not an adherence test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring conformance of observed play mix to the recommended opener and treating it as evidence of execution quality
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as descriptive with no outcome comparison; single-game horizon; roughly 100 possessions per game; CUT and PNR muted by tagger floor; mechanism unclear (E_unclear); no validation recorded; the recommended opener was not rank-1 for 4 of 8 sides.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether series-level AVOID share predicts losing
failed_approaches.why: Series-level n=50 gave p=0.07, underpowered (about 80 series needed for p<0.05 per the record); team-quality confound not removed; game-level p-value inflated by non-independent games; classified A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranked playsheet counter validation (BEST > SECOND > AVOID predicting H2 scoring)
failed_approaches.why: Full-rank Spearman null (p=0.0997); the significant pairwise BEST vs AVOID result is not a full-rank confirmation; leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample and drift all recorded as limits; mechanism unclear (E_unclear).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-winner claim from an LLM adaptation batch ('9/10 adaptation predicts winning')
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: 706 findings with n<5, winners not looked up in source data, invented scores, LLM arithmetic; SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risk recorded.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix against series or game winning.

Earlier attempts in this project to link play-type strategy measures to winning either returned a null or underpowered result (SF-CHT-039 at n=50, p=0.07; SF-APPS-018 full-rank Spearman null) or were classified as artifacts (SF-APPA-008).
Team-quality confounding was recorded as a blocking problem for series-level strategy-to-winning claims (SF-CHT-039).
Observed-versus-recommended mix conformance has been measured descriptively, with large deviations and mechanism unclear (SF-APPS-017).
Measurement limits were recorded for play-type tagging: a tagger floor muting some play types (SF-APPS-017) and low measurement reliability (SF-APPS-018).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence predicts winning in any sample, since no adherence-to-outcome test was retrieved.
The effect size of adherence on series outcome, or the power for a given effect.
Whether the suppression-conditional recommendation is itself valid out of sample.
Whether the recorded results for related questions would hold on the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data described in the task.
The series-level sample size for the current 54-series design; retrieved records used n=50 and n=10, not this dataset.
own_inferences: With 54 series and a winning base rate near 0.5, the power to detect a modest adherence effect is low. The retrieved SF-CHT-039 record (n=50, p=0.07, about 80 needed) suggests the planned sample is roughly at or below what would be needed for a conventional threshold.

If the recommended mix is derived from the same play-by-play and outcome-correlated data used to score adherence, the adherence measure is partly constructed from the outcome (LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD), so a positive association could be produced by construction.
Team quality is probably the dominant driver of both adherence (good teams execute plans) and winning, so an unadjusted association would be confounded.
The question 'adherence predicts winning' conflates suppression quality with execution; a team that follows a good recommendation may still lose on talent, and a team that deviates may still win.
uncertainties: The exact definition of the suppression-conditional recommended mix and of adherence is not stated in the task; the retrieved records do not describe it.
Whether the 54 series units are independent across seasons (team and coach overlap) is unknown.
The tagger's coverage of play types (CUT, PNR) in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 files is not verified.
The 2025-26 playoff data are partial before 2026-06-21, so the playoff component of the sample is not fixed as of the question date (2026-06-16).
Retrieval returned four records, none testing this exact question; the search depth beyond these was not used.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the question looked like a standard prediction test using 54 series. The retrieved records show that earlier series-level strategy-to-winning tests in this project were underpowered (SF-CHT-039), confounded by team quality, or classified as artifacts (SF-APPA-008), and that adherence measurement itself was descriptive with unclear mechanism (SF-APPS-017). This supports not running the confirmatory test as posed and instead restricting to a pre-registered design with out-of-sample validation and explicit power.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series units give low power for a modest adherence effect; the retrieved n=50 series test reached p=0.07 and the record states about 80 series are needed for p<0.05.
The recommended mix and the adherence score are derived from the same play-by-play data used to label winners, so the measure may encode the outcome.
Team quality drives both execution of a plan and winning; no retrieved design removes this confound (SF-CHT-039).
Play-type tagging has a floor that mutes some plays (SF-APPS-017), and reliability of the measured mix was recorded as low (SF-APPS-018).

prior_work.summary: Earlier records address adjacent questions: descriptive mix conformance (SF-APPS-017), series-level AVOID share vs winning (SF-CHT-039), ranked playsheet counter validation (SF-APPS-018), and a winning-claim audit (SF-APPA-008). None tests adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix against winning, so the exact question is not answered, though the adjacent results constrain it.

risks.text: 54 series is at or below the roughly 80 series the record in SF-CHT-039 cites for a conventional threshold at a comparable effect.
Recommendation and adherence scoring from the same data as the outcome; SF-APPS-018 flagged leakage.
Team quality confounds execution and winning; recorded in SF-CHT-039.
Tagger floor mutes CUT and PNR (SF-APPS-017); low measurement reliability recorded in SF-APPS-018.
Tagger coverage floor limits which play types can be measured in the adherence mix (SF-APPS-017).
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons with changing rotations and play styles; drift flagged in SF-APPS-018.
Several sub-claims (pairwise BEST vs AVOID, Kruskal-Wallis, trigger accuracy) in earlier work would multiply comparisons if repeated here (SF-APPS-018).
Series winning is about 0.5 by construction; a favourite-based baseline (seed or rating) is needed to judge predictive lift.
No placebo or negative-control mix was recorded in the retrieved records to separate adherence from general good play.
Series winners must be taken from the box-score or series records, not inferred; SF-APPA-008 found LLM-inferred winners.
Derived possession records and point costs have been mis-computed in earlier batches (SF-APPA-008).

design.estimand: Not proceeding with the confirmatory estimand as posed. Minimum viable estimand: the association between out-of-sample adherence to a pre-specified recommended mix and series win, adjusted for team strength (e.g., pre-series rating), reported with a confidence interval.
design.unit: Series (one per matchup), with games as nested observations only for descriptive use.
design.sample: 54 series from 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as available; 2025-26 playoff series only counted once complete (after 2026-06-21). The recommendation must be frozen before scoring adherence.
design.power: Not achievable at 54 series for a modest effect. Report the minimum detectable effect explicitly; the earlier record suggests about 80 series for p<0.05 at a comparable effect, so the test is expected to be underpowered.
design.controls: Adjust for pre-series team rating and seed; use the recommendation fitted on seasons before the scored series (no same-series data); placebo mix from a random or shuffled recommendation; exclude partial 2025-26 playoff data.
design.falsification: Shuffled-recommendation placebo should show no association; if adherence predicts winning equally under the placebo, the claim fails.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary contrast (adherence to recommendation vs series win, adjusted for team rating). Treat BEST vs AVOID pairwise and trigger accuracy as secondary, with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Count the question as supported only if the pre-registered primary effect is positive with a 95% interval excluding zero, survives the placebo check, and holds out of sample; otherwise report as inconclusive or rejected, not as a finding.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-06-16 (2025-26 playoffs partial before 2026-06-21); frozen recommendation version recorded with a hash.

methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series or game winning with 54 series units?
How should adherence be measured and validated against a recommendation derived from the same data?
What leakage, sample size, and base-rate risks threaten a test of recommendation adherence and winning?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
